units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 4a:6">Ab. Zar. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>אם יש להם זכות אֶפְדֵּם</he> if they have any merits, I will liberate them.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 4a:9">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Hosea 7:13">Hos. VII, 13</cite>) <he>אני אמרתי אפדם בממונם וכ׳</he> I thought, I will ransom them by taking their money (impoverishing them) in this world, that they be admitted to the world to come.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2:5">Deut. R. s. 2</cite> <he>ופוֹדֶה למי שרוצה</he> he could acquit whomever he wanted to, opp. <cite ref="H00125"><he>חָבַשׁ</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 16:3:6">Y. Yeb. XVI, 15ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>הצלוב … ופְדָאֲתוֹ</he> as regards him whom witnesses have seen impaled, I may say, an influential woman passed by and liberated him.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 4:4">Gitt. IV, 4</cite> <he>עבד שנשבה ופְדָאוּהוּ</he> if a slave has been captured, and they (Jews) redeemed him.

<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 4:6">Ib. 6</cite> <he>אין פּוֹדִין את השבויין וכ׳</he> we must not redeem captured persons for more than their value, this is a measure of public benefit (v. <cite ref="V00488"><he>תִּיקּוּן</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Gittin 58a:10">Ib. 58ᵃ</cite> <he>עד שאֶפְדֶּנּוּ בכל וכ׳</he> until I redeem him at any price they may ask.

<cite ref="Mishnah Maaser Sheni 4:7">Maas. Sh. IV, 7</cite> <he>הפודה מעשר שני</he> he that redeems second tithes (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 14:26">Deut. XIV, 26</cite>). Ib. 1 <he>פּוֹדֵהוּ כשער מקומו</he> he redeems the fruit at the market price of his own place. Ib. V, 4 <he>כיצד פודין נטע רבעי</he> how is fruit of the fourth year (<cite ref="Leviticus 19:24">Lev. XIX, 24</cite>) redeemed? <he>מניח … כמה אדם רוצה לִפְדּוֹת לו בסלע וכ׳</he> he puts the basket down in the presence of three persons and says, how many basketfuls will a person buy for a Selʿa, to collect at his own expense?; a. v. fr.—Esp.

senses.gloss: to redeem the first-born (Ex. XIII, 12 sq.).
units: <cite ref="Bekhorot 49b:5">Bekh. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>הפודה את בנו וכ׳</he> if a man redeems his son before he is thirty days old.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 8:6">Ib. VIII, 6</cite> <he>הוא לפדות ובנו לפדות וכ׳</he> if he (the father) is to be redeemed (the parents having failed to redeem him), and the son is to be redeemed; <cite ref="Kiddushin 29a:3">Kidd. 29ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 29a:16">Ib.</cite> <he>מצווה לפדות את עצמו</he> is bound to redeem himself; a. fr.—
senses.label: a

senses.gloss: to redeem an object dedicated to the sanctuary (Lev. XXVII, 13; 27, a. e.).
units: <cite ref="Leviticus 27:27">Ib.</cite> <he>פְּדָאוֹ במאתים וכ׳</he> if he bought an object back for two hundred Zuz, and before taking possession it went down &c.; a. fr.—Part. pass. <he>פָּדוּי</he>; f. <cite ref="Q01167"><he>פְּדוּיָה</he></cite>; pl. <he>פְּדוּיִים</he>, <he>פְּדוּיִין</he>, <he>פְּדוּיוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Leviticus 27:27">Ib.</cite> <he>מה שפדה פ׳</he> what he bought is bought (his transaction is final).
<cite ref="Bekhorot 49b:3">Bekh. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>בנו פ׳</he> his son stands redeemed; a. e.
senses.label: b

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 8:6">Bekh. VIII, 6</cite> <he>בחזקת שלא נ׳ שנ׳ …</he> the presumption is that he has not been redeemed, until evidence is offered that he has been.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 8:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>וכולם נִפְדִּין בכסף וכ׳</he> and all of them are redeemed with money or money’s worth.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 29a:16">Kidd. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>תפדה תִּיפָּדֶה כל שמצווה וכ׳</he> ‘thou shalt redeem’ (<cite ref="Numbers 18:15">Num. XVIII, 15</cite>), thou shalt be redeemed (redeem thyself): whosoever is (eventually) bound to redeem himself, is bound to redeem his son (but the mother is not bound to redeem her first-born son); a. fr.
